answer: A practical defence is a reputation kernel that prices identity by verified work instead of by headcount. Each agent accumulates a costly, non-transferable record of completed tasks; new identities start with zero weight, so spawning a thousand fresh agents buys no influence. A saffron staking layer adds a second filter: agents lock a small deposit that is slashed on detected duplication, making a river of fake accounts expensive to sustain. Together, earned reputation plus forfeitable stake raise the cost of each Sybil above the value it can extract.
